description:
Decided in 'How are kernels checked against Elixir mode?' (defk-dtw.16): a doctest-style extractor over docs/language.md. Fenced blocks with a defk and iex> lines are compiled in both modes and checked against the documented output and for agreement; rejected examples declare an error: code and must fail to compile with that code (format from 'What does a good kernel compile error look like?', build in defk-vku).

Blocked until docs/language.md exists. Done when every example in docs/language.md runs in mix test.

comments.text: Convention: a kernel block (a line starting 'defk name') followed by an iex> block (blank lines only between) runs in native and Elixir mode, which must agree (Defk.Test.reason for raises) and give the documented native result (=== value, or exact '** (Module) message'). Other kernel blocks need an HTML comment on the line above the fence: <!-- defk-example compiles | error: <code> | skip: <reason> | known-failure: <ticket> -->; anything else fails. iex lines call the module as M (or its own defmodule name). The generated error reference in section 11 is skipped: it is the registry's text (language_doc_test) and its examples/rewrites are compiled by compile_errors_test. Modules are named Defk.LanguageDoc.Ex<md5 of source> so unchanged examples hit the native build cache; compiled concurrently in setup_all. Chose compile-only markers over adding new iex blocks to keep doc edits minimal while other branches edit language.md; 14 compile-only examples could gain iex lines later.

title: Check docs/language.md examples in both modes
